newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-TURKEY CELEBRATES FENERBAHCE'S WIN AGAINST UNITED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TURKEY CELEBRATES FENERBAHCE'S WIN AGAINST UNITED.

text.p: Fenerbahce's historic win against English champions Manchester United at Old Trafford dominated Turkey's usually grim agenda on Thursday as the whole country celebrated with joy and surprise.
"Fenerbahce goes down in history!" screamed the banner headline of the conservative Sabah daily of the Istanbul team's 1-0 win -- United's first home defeat in 40 years of European competition.
"The miracle happened," said the mass-selling Hurriyet. "The Fenerbahce legend!" exclaimed the liberal Milliyet.

Turks poured onto the rain-dampened streets, shouting, firing guns and sounding their car horns even before Wednesday night's European Champions' League match was over and continued chanting and celebrating well into the night.
The news pushed aside stories of Turkey's 12-year-old fight with rebel Kurds, who recently stepped up their assault on security forces with a wave of suicide bombings.
The minute the match was over, President Suleyman Demirel sent a note of congratulations to the team. He was quickly followed by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and Sports Minister Bahattin Seker.
"Your victory has overwhelmed the whole nation with joy," said Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller in a message to gregarious Fenerbahce chairman Ali Sen.
With Fenerbahce now off the bottom of Group C in the European Champions' league, fast-talking Sen quickly promised more of the same.
"Everybody laughed at us when we said we would become European champions. But we will make this happen," Sen said.
Fenerbahce are two points behind United with four points after four matches. Leaders Juventus have 10 points.
Each player earned some $10,500 in bonuses for the win, and newspapers reported that Turkish firms were queuing up to shower further rewards on the players.
Overzealous celebrations after Fenerbahce's victory took their usual toll on the unsuspecting Turkish public.
A 25-year-old man firing randomly out of his window in jubilation shot a woman in the stomach and her 10-month-old baby in the feet, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
The mother and son, who were were sitting on their balcony at the time, were rushed to hospital.
In a separate incident, an 18-year-old was shot in the neck by a stray bullet while peering over his balcony to watch ecstatic Fenerbahce fans celebrating in the streets.
Turkish media reported with delight the United fans' dejection at the loss, and triumphantly cited British media stories writing Fenerbahce off against the English champions.
Turks were already overjoyed at Tuesday night's win by another Istanbul team, Besiktas, against Legia Warsaw to reach the third round of the UEFA Cup for the first time.

Thirsty for more victories, newspapers were looking ahead to Thursday's European Cup Winners' Cup tie between Galatasaray and Paris St Germain. The Turks have a 4-2 advantage over the French champions after the first leg in Istanbul.
"Go on you lions, write another legend!" urged the sports daily Fanatik.
